chunks: If someone who knows the prophethood of Musa (peace be upon him) through the miracles indicating his prophethood, does not properly reflect on the miracles apparent on Isa (peace be upon him) and our Messenger Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family), it is not necessary to conclude that he did not know those miracles, because it is not impossible that he is aware of them and the manner of their indication, even if he does not know these miracles and the manner of their indication has been unclear to him.
ai.seo_question: How can one be aware of miracles without explicitly recognizing them as such?
ai.summary: Al-Tusi employs this epistemological nuance to address the doubt surrounding the Imam's occultation, arguing that the absence of explicit, undeniable proof for the current Imam does not equate to ignorance, as one may possess latent knowledge of the signs without fully comprehending their specific application. This distinction between mere awareness and deep, reflective understanding serves to validate the faith of those who follow the Imam despite the hidden nature of his authority. It underscores the Shia principle that certainty can be derived from varied degrees of evidence, preventing the dismissal of the Imamate due to the lack of universally obvious miracles.
